title: Introduce gpu_nodepool_migration operator and scoped IAM grantor for safe state moves
author: Maya Chen
description:
Problem / Context:
Private installs that need to move GPU node pools between subnet groups, or rebind nodepools to different tenant-scoped TFState boundaries, frequently rely on manual state surgery and ad-hoc IAM modifications. This creates outages during migrations and increases blast-radius when operators need elevated privileges.

What this PR does:
- Adds a new reusable Terraform module modules/gpu_nodepool_migration that codifies a safe migration workflow for GPU nodepools (create-new-nodepool -> drain -> reprovision workloads -> retire-old-nodepool). The module exposes hooks for pre/post migration actions and emits a state_anchor resource to record migration checkpoints.
- Introduces modules/iam/grantor which defines a narrowly-scoped IAM role and policies (AssumeRole-only by installer service account, ephemeral session duration, least-privileged actions limited to nodepool lifecycle: create, tag, attach-subnet, cordon/uncordon via cloud provider node API). This avoids granting global admin to the installer during upgrades.
- Adds network enforcement variables (subnet_affinity_policy) to modules/network to optionally enforce subnet binding for GPU nodepools and to compute candidate subnets for the new pool during migration.
- Adds a migration orchestration example in examples/private/migration/ showing a two-phase, canary-first migration runbook that uses the tfstate snapshotter and the state_anchor produced by the module.
- Adds acceptance tests and a small e2e job in ci/ that exercises canary migration on a local KIND cluster (mock provider), plus unit tests for IAM policy generation.

Why this approach:
- Keeps migration logic in Terraform so operator intent and rollback checkpoints are part of source control.
- Minimizes the time any operator needs elevated privileges by scoping an ephemeral grantor.
- Provides reproducible, auditable migration checkpoints via state_anchor so the private-installer can roll forward or safely rollback to a known state.

Migration plan and rollout:
1) Deploy head_branch to staging using the example runbook; verify state_anchor is emitted after canary migration.
2) Run the IAM policy reviewer (script included) to verify grantor privileges are within expected bounds.
3) Gradually apply the module to additional tenant stacks.
4) After full rollout, retire grantor roles via a follow-up PR that drops the temporary assume role binding.

Rollback guidance:
- Each migration emits a state_anchor with a timestamp and the old pool resource IDs. Reverting to the previous anchor is documented in examples/private/migration/rollback.md and implemented as a small helper script (scripts/rollback_to_anchor.sh).

Notes / non-goals:
- This PR does not change runtime serving code or autoscaler behavior. The module focuses on safe infra migration paths and IAM scoping.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module and README
- [x] IAM policy templates and test cases
- [x] Network affinity option and documentation
- [x] Example runbook + rollback script
- [x] CI jobs exercising plan/lint/unit tests

review_comments:
Ava Patel: Please tighten the grantor policy to remove any iam:PassRole and restrict tag/label actions to the nodepool resource namespace only. Also add a test for stale anchor cleanup.

Maya Chen (author): Good catch — removed iam:PassRole and replaced it with a scoped sts:AssumeRole only. Added a unit test that asserts the anchor TTL and a cleanup helper in scripts/.

Luis Gomez: The subnet_affinity_policy should default to permissive for existing installs to avoid accidental failures. Suggest adding a warning in the module README.

Maya Chen: Added default = "permissive" and a clear README warning and upgrade note.

Sophie Ito: CI shows a lint failure on tflint rules for tag naming on initial run. Re-run after fix.

Maya Chen: Fixed tag format and pushed patch. CI passed on rerun.

merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge by Ava Patel after approvals from Luis Gomez and Sophie Ito. Merge commit message summarises module, grantor role, and migration runbook. No follow-up blockers assigned.
release_notes:
- Added gpu_nodepool_migration Terraform module to orchestrate safe nodepool migrations for private installs.
- Introduced iam/grantor module: ephemeral, least-privileged grantor role for installer-driven nodepool operations.
- Network subnet_affinity_policy option to control subnet binding during migrations.
- Example runbook and rollback script included for staged rollouts and safety.
notes_for_ops: Staging verification required before prod rollout. Run examples/private/migration/verify.sh to confirm state_anchor emission. Remove grantor role with follow-up PR once migration window completes.
security_notes: Grantor policy deliberately minimizes privileges; review script provided (scripts/verify_grantor_policy.sh). No iam:PassRole is included. Recorded grantor assume events should be audited in cloud audit logs.
extra_context: This PR pairs with a small private-installer change (private-installer#482) that will call the state_anchor helper during canary runs. Coordinator work item: ENG-2048 tracks automation to retire grantor roles post-migration.
